title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Assumption University's residential campus in Worcester.

cards.title: The Campus Gateway
cards.subtitle: Salisbury Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk south from the main entrance to reach the Worcester Art Museum and historic residential architecture lining this primary campus artery.
cards.short_summary: The primary thoroughfare connecting Assumption University to the cultural institutions of downtown Worcester.
cards.evidence_claim: Assumption University is located at 500 Salisbury Street, which serves as the main access road for the campus.
cards.access_notes: Public city street with sidewalk access directly from the university's main gate.

cards.title: Local Dining Hub
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Visit local favorites like Blue Jeans Pizza for thin-crust pies, a staple for students heading off-campus for a meal.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial corridor featuring a high density of student-friendly restaurants and local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: Blue Jeans Pizza at 270 Park Ave is identified as a favorite eatery for Assumption students.
cards.access_notes: Commercial street with various business hours; generally accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Restaurant Row
cards.subtitle: Highland Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by The Sole Proprietor or The Boynton for classic Worcester dining experiences frequently visited by the college community.
cards.short_summary: A historic street known for its diverse culinary options and proximity to several Worcester colleges.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sole Proprietor and The Boynton on Highland Street are listed as recommended local favorites for students.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare with numerous restaurants; check individual business hours.

cards.title: Industrial Revitalization
cards.subtitle: Grove Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head to The Fix Burger Bar for custom burgers in a renovated industrial space, a popular spot for student weekend outings.
cards.short_summary: A corridor featuring repurposed industrial buildings now housing trendy eateries and professional offices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fix Burger Bar at 108 Grove St is highlighted as a creative dining destination for the campus community.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via car or bus; businesses typically open for lunch and dinner.

cards.title: Retail & Essentials
cards.subtitle: Gold Star Boulevard Corridor
cards.notes: Access major retailers and quick-service dining like Starbucks and Panera Bread, serving the large student population in North Worcester.
cards.short_summary: A high-traffic commercial district providing essential shopping and dining services to nearby universities.
cards.evidence_claim: Gold Star Boulevard is a major trade area with retailers like Starbucks and Panera, located in close proximity to Assumption.
cards.access_notes: Major commercial road with ample parking for retail visitors.

cards.title: Restaurant Row
cards.subtitle: Shrewsbury Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore 'Restaurant Row' for a wide array of cafes and pizzerias, including the unique Root & Press cafe and bookstore.
cards.short_summary: Worcester's premier dining destination, famous for its Italian heritage and diverse restaurant selection.
cards.evidence_claim: Shrewsbury Street is known as 'Restaurant Row' and is a recommended destination for Assumption students.
cards.access_notes: Public street; Root & Press is located at 156 Shrewsbury Street.

cards.title: The Healthy Choice
cards.subtitle: Chandler Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit Nu Kitchen for healthy lifestyle eats or Nancy Chang's for fresh Asian cuisine, both located along this busy transit route.
cards.short_summary: A key east-west corridor connecting several campus communities with a focus on health-conscious dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Nu Kitchen and Nancy Chang's on Chandler Street are listed as favorite student eateries.
cards.access_notes: Served by WRTA Route 10, connecting Assumption and Worcester State.

cards.title: Historic Student Living
cards.subtitle: June Street Neighborhood
cards.notes: Walk through this neighborhood known for its high concentration of historic homes and student-friendly residential environment.
cards.short_summary: A residential area popular with college students due to its walkability and historic character.
cards.evidence_claim: The June Street neighborhood is rated as a top college-friendly place to live in MA with a high concentration of historic residences.
cards.source_title: June Street Worcester, MA Neighborhood Profile
cards.access_notes: Public residential neighborhood; walkable from nearby commercial areas.

cards.title: The Urban Core
cards.subtitle: Main Street Corridor
cards.notes: Engage with the community at the Assumption Center or visit local shops in this diverse and revitalizing urban district.
cards.short_summary: The central spine of Worcester, hosting community centers and diverse local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Assumption Center is located at 16 Vineyard St, just off Main Street, serving the Main South neighborhood.
cards.access_notes: Public urban corridor; the Assumption Center offers various community programs.

cards.title: North Worcester Link
cards.subtitle: West Boylston Street Corridor
cards.notes: Access regional services and the Greendale area, including the site of the original Assumption College campus.
cards.short_summary: A major northern artery connecting the university area to the Greendale neighborhood and regional transit.
cards.evidence_claim: West Boylston Street is a primary route in North Worcester, passing through the Greendale area near the original campus site.
cards.source_title: Worcester neighborhood shaped for generations by company
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; serves as a key route for commuters and local residents.
